content: PCAF, also referred to as KAT2B (K lysine acetyltransferase 2B), is a human gene that encodes a transcriptional coactivator associated with the tumor suppressor protein p53. Structure PCAF contains multiple functional domains that can operate independently or synergistically. These include distinct acetyltransferase and E3 ubiquitin ligase domains, as well as a bromodomain that facilitates interactions with other proteins. Additionally, PCAF has specific sites for its own acetylation and ubiquitination. Function CBP (CREB-binding protein) and p300 are large nuclear proteins that interact with various sequence-specific factors involved in cellular growth and differentiation, such as c-Jun and the adenoviral oncoprotein E1A. The protein encoded by the PCAF gene associates with p300/CBP and exhibits both in vitro and in vivo binding activity with these proteins. PCAF competes with E1A for binding sites on p300/CBP. It also possesses histone acetyltransferase activity, targeting core histones and nucleosome core particles, which underscores its direct role in transcriptional regulation. Regulation The acetyltransferase activity and subcellular localization of PCAF are regulated through its own acetylation. PCAF can undergo autoacetylation or be acetylated by p300. Acetylation promotes its migration to the nucleus and enhances its acetyltransferase activity. Conversely, PCAF interacts with and is deacetylated by HDAC3 (histone deacetylase 3), which reduces its acetyltransferase activity and leads to its cytoplasmic localization. Protein Interactions PCAF forms complexes with numerous proteins that modulate its activity. For instance, it is recruited by ATF (activating transcription factor) to acetylate histones and facilitate the transcription of ATF4 target genes. Targets PCAF’s acetyltransferase activity targets a variety of proteins, including transcription factors such as Fli1 and p53, as well as multiple histone residues. Additionally, Hdm2, a ubiquitin ligase that targets p53, has been identified as a substrate of PCAF’s ubiquitin-ligase activity. Interactions PCAF has been shown to interact with the following proteins: BRCA2 CTNNB1 (β-catenin) CREBBP (CBP) EVI1 HNF1A IRF1 IRF2 KLF13 Mdm2 Myc NCOA1 POLR2A (RNA polymerase II subunit A) RBPJ TCF3 TRRAP TWIST1
